quiz.stem: The milk has big bubbles on top after steaming. What went wrong?

options.text: The milk was too cold to start with
Too much air went in, too late
The milk spun for too long

quiz.explanation: Air goes in early, while the milk is cold, so the spin has time to break it into fine bubbles. Air let in near the end stays as big bubbles on top.

quiz.stem: When do you stop letting air into the milk?

options.text: As soon as the steam is on
When the jug is too hot to hold
When the jug is about hand-warm
When the milk has doubled in volume

quiz.explanation: Stretch while the milk is cold, until the jug is about hand-warm, then sink the tip and let the spin polish it. Stop steaming before the jug is too hot to hold.

quiz.stem: Why do you swirl the jug before pouring?

options.text: To keep the foam folded into the milk, so it pours glossy

quiz.explanation: Foam rises and separates as milk stands. Swirling keeps it folded in, so the pour is one glossy texture rather than milk followed by a cap of foam.
